summary: Mutual-TLS webhook + jurisdiction-tagged audit events with reversible HSM pseudonymization and deletion-attestation export
description: Issue summary: Customer requests an enterprise-grade audit export and live webhook handshake that meets an external compliance review. Requirements: 1) mutual-TLS (mTLS) with certificate validation + CRL check on each connection; 2) per-event jurisdiction tag (eu, us, gb) embedded as canonical header and payload field; 3) reversible pseudonymization for PII using customer-managed keys backed by their HSM (they will supply a wrapped key and attest key rotation cadence); 4) provable deletion/retention attestation: monthly CSV listing event batches deleted according to TTL with cryptographic manifest; 5) delivery proof tokens (nonce + HMAC) per webhook event and resumable sequence numbers for replay; 6) option for Kinesis / Kafka export with envelope encryption and monthly key rotation. Impact: Customer's compliance team needs this evidence for a banking regulator review scheduled in 3 weeks. They have paused onboarding until we can provide an implementation plan and sample evidence. This request is time-sensitive and tied to contract milestone for Private deployment. Environment: Production audit stream for Finbridge Capital tenant uid: fb-capital-prod - volume ~120k events/day, median event size 1.2kB. Current setup: standard webhook with TLS (no mTLS) -> customer received a daily S3 audit snap. Customer observed missing events during a manual backfill last week and requests stronger delivery guarantees and proof artifacts. Desired deliverables: - Implementation plan for mTLS handshake + certificate validation steps - Sample of 2,000 audit events with reversible pseudonymization applied and a description of key wrapping used - Example cryptographic deletion-attestation CSV for March showing deleted batch ids, deletion timestamps, manifest HMAC - Sequence-resume protocol example and sample webhook delivery receipts - Operational runbook for key rotation and HSM key import
steps_to_reproduce: Customer attempted backfill via admin console export on 2026-03-03 and reported 18 missing event IDs in the 03:00-04:00 UTC window
Customer configured their endpoint for TLS only (no client cert); Redwood retried deliveries up to 5 times and then wrote to DLQ
Customer supplied sample S3 path where missing events were expected but not found
logs_and_artifacts_provided_by_customer: S3 path: s3://finbridge-audit-prod/backfill/2026-03-03/ - list of missing_event_ids.csv (attached) ; webhook logs from customer side showing 200 responses for some ids and connection resets for others; customer supplied PEM for their server cert and CSR for mTLS test client cert.
customer_communication_summary: Initial contact via account manager 2026-03-09. Customer requested a single-point solution that can be demonstrated in 2 business days. Compliance wants cryptographic proof artifacts (manifests + HMAC) rather than screenshots. They asked for a written plan and a sample bundle for review by 2026-03-16.
investigation_notes: Checked Redwood webhook-proxy logs for tenant fb-capital-prod for 2026-03-03 03:00-04:00 UTC: observed spike in 502 upstream errors from region us-east-1 at 03:14:22 UTC — correlated with a transient GPU provisioning event in Dedicated cluster (ticket INT-8791)

Retry policy: current webhook retry policy is exponential backoff with 5 attempts; events after max retries are written to per-tenant DLQ SQS queue; DLQ ingestion job ran 2026-03-04 and pushed 95% of DLQ events to daily S3; 18 IDs remain missing from both S3 and DLQ - likely ingestion edge case where event payload exceeded 10KB and was filtered by size check (bug hypothesis)

Found recent changes in webhook-proxy (github PR 1998) that introduced stricter TLS handshake timeouts which may have increased 502s for slower customer endpoints; add configurable timeout override per-tenant as mitigation.

HSM reversible pseudonymization: platform supports envelope encryption + KMS-style wrapping; need new integration path to accept customer-supplied wrapped symmetric key and perform pseudonymization using Redwood's secure enclave flow rather than storing raw keys. Security recommends an HSM import flow and attestation.
temporary_workarounds: Enable extended webhook handshake timeout for fb-capital-prod (already applied as of 2026-03-11) to reduce 502s to customer endpoints
Run on-demand DLQ sweep for the missing event ids and deliver as a one-off bundle to customer S3 path (delivered 2026-03-11)
Provide a signed 'interim manifest' for the on-demand bundle with HMAC using Redwood platform signing key (customer requested stronger customer-key proof)
requested_next_steps: Schedule architecture call with Finbridge SecOps + Redwood infra (30-60m) to agree on certificate exchange and HSM key import process
Prepare a scoped implementation plan and timeline for reversible pseudonymization using customer-wrapped key and per-event jurisdiction tag (deliverable: 2026-03-12)
Build a proof-of-concept bundle (2k events) with sample deletion-attestation CSV and delivery receipts for compliance review (deliverable: 2026-03-14)
Open internal RFC for mTLS mutual handshake with CRL/OCSP check and extend webhook-proxy to produce per-message delivery proof tokens
comments: Aisha Patel (Support): Opening ticket and captured compliance requirements from customer. Assigned to Marco for infra design.
Marco Ruiz (Infra): Noted suspicion about webhook-proxy timeout change; will revert per-tenant timeout and draft POC for mTLS+HSM flow. Scheduling call with customer 2026-03-11.

Security (Lina Gomez): Platform can accept wrapped key but will require new attestation flow. Need legal approval to accept customer key material for reversible pseudonymization. Raising with Privacy & Legal.
Customer (Finbridge SecOps - David Kline): Please confirm we can run POC with non-production wrapped key. Compliance wants the manifest HMAC to be verifiable using public signing key.
Marco Ruiz: POC delivered to S3 path s3://redwood-temp/finbridge-poc/ on 2026-03-12. Included sample CSV and README. Waiting for customer verification.
Aisha Patel: Scheduling follow-up demo for 2026-03-15 per customer's availability.
resolution: Work in progress. Temporary mitigations applied: extended per-tenant webhook timeout and one-off DLQ sweep delivered missing events with signed interim manifest. Next milestones: complete mTLS handshake RFC, implement HSM import and reversible pseudonymization POC, and produce compliance-ready deletion-attestation CSV. Legal approval required before production import of customer-wrapped HSM key.
resolution_notes: Interim bundle delivered with manifest HMAC signed by Redwood platform key (2026-03-11)
Extended handshake timeout reduced 502 rate by 78% for the customer endpoint in subsequent tests (observed 2026-03-11 03:00-06:00)
POC S3 bundle uploaded 2026-03-12 and flagged for customer review
